messages.subject: time-stratification error (anonymised)
parts:
Answer to a question about an error in time-stratification, anonymised. Posting for google-ability.

Cheers,
Nick



I am XX, a Ph.D. candidate at the Department of XX, University of XX. I am writing to you to ask a question.
Indeed, I am analyzing a mtDNA dataset on a XX species, and very interested in calculating some biogeography analyses such as DEC, Divalike and Bayarea tests using your excellent package (BioGeoBEARS). I am attaching all of my input file
Therefore, I have run a time-stratified analysis in your new package and I received the following error message:

> # Run to check inputs
> BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
> # Divide the tree up by strata
> BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces
1- top: 0, bot: 0.5, rel_bot: 0.5

2- top: 0.5, bot: 0.9, rel_bot: 0.4

  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed


Despite my tries, I could not solve this problem.

I was wondering if you could kindly help me in this case.

Thank you so much,

2. Phylogeny problem:

Your mtDNA tree looks like it is probably a specimen tree -- that is, it is a phylogeny of the mtDNA locus (a gene tree or locus tree), rather than a tree of species/populations.  This is a problem for this reason:

BioGeoBEARS: OTUs of the phylogeny should be species/populations, not specimens
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#no_specimen_trees

If you want to do biogeography on a mtDNA specimen tree, this is possible with a simplified model, basically BAYAREALIKE*+a-d-e, which is basically the Markov-k (Mk) model, i.e. a simple model for an unordered character.  Shorter version: you can treat biogeography like an standard unordered character.

The Mk model as BAYAREALIKE*+a-d-e
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#BAYAREALIKEa



3. Phylogeny problem:

The other issue with the phylogeny is that not all of the tips come up to time=0 at the present.  One clade is 0.013633 higher than the rest of the tips.  This means that BioGeoBEARS thinks all of the lower tips are fossils, which is unlikely to be true!  The practical impact is minimal if you set cut_fossils=FALSE in the section_the_tree() function, but it's better to sort this out before analysis.

General advice on dated trees:

Use dated phylogenies
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#use_dated_phylogenies

Cheers, 
Nick
